papers.justification: This paper focuses on the application of transformers in computer vision and does not directly address the theoretical expressivity of transformers as the seed papers do.

papers.title: Prompting a Pretrained Transformer Can Be a Universal Approximator
papers.justification: This paper directly addresses the theoretical expressivity of transformers through the lens of prompting and prefix-tuning, which is closely related to the expressivity of transformer encoders discussed in the seed papers.

papers.title: Practical Computational Power of Linear Transformers and Their Recurrent and Self-Referential Extensions
papers.justification: This paper directly addresses neural algorithmic reasoning using auto-regressive Transformers with linearized attention, which is closely related to the expressivity of Transformers as discussed in the seed papers.

papers.title: Size and Depth Separation in Approximating Benign Functions with Neural Networks
papers.justification: This paper focuses on the approximation capabilities of neural networks for benign functions, which is tangentially related to the expressivity of transformers but does not directly address the theoretical expressivity of transformers as discussed in the seed papers.

papers.title: Transformers, parallel computation, and logarithmic depth
papers.justification: This paper directly addresses the computational depth and parallelism of transformers, which is closely related to the expressivity of transformers as discussed in the seed papers.

papers.title: Influence Patterns for Explaining Information Flow in BERT
papers.justification: This paper directly addresses the information flow within BERT, which is a type of transformer model, and thus relates to the expressivity of transformers.

papers.title: Exponentially Improving the Complexity of Simulating the Weisfeiler-Lehman Test with Graph Neural Networks
papers.justification: This paper focuses on the complexity of simulating the Weisfeiler-Lehman test with graph neural networks and does not directly address the expressivity of transformers.

papers.title: Simulating weighted automata over sequences and trees with transformers
papers.justification: This paper directly addresses neural algorithmic reasoning using transformers, which is closely related to understanding the computational capabilities and expressivity of transformers as discussed in the seed papers.

papers.title: CAT-probing: A Metric-based Approach to Interpret How Pre-trained Models for Programming Language Attend Code Structure
papers.justification: This paper focuses on interpreting pre-trained models for programming language code structure and does not directly address the theoretical expressivity of transformers as defined by the seed papers.

papers.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
papers.justification: This paper directly addresses the development and application of transformer-based models, which is central to the research topic on the theoretical expressivity of transformers.

papers.title: Chain of Thought Empowers Transformers to Solve Inherently Serial Problems
papers.justification: This paper shares the problem domain of reasoning tasks but does not directly address the expressivity of transformers.

papers.title: Universal Transformers
papers.justification: This candidate paper focuses on RNNs and their sequential processing, which is somewhat tangentially related to the expressivity of transformers, a parallel processing architecture.
